scope: Written formulas,owner decisions and primary publications only. No repository code,existingtests or liveapp outputs were inspected for this review. Attached screen-register worked/app-result fields were excluded from expected-answer derivation.

formula_checks.name: buildBudgetState
formula_checks.why: Missing stored expenses become zero and therefore produce a positive projected saving without a budget.
formula_checks.should_be: Refuse projected saving until income and budget completeness are known.

formula_checks.name: plannedMonthlySpend
formula_checks.why: Adds the actual calendar-year plan and divides by twelve; an explicitly dated annual bill is counted once on top of the recurring typed figure. This is an annual average, not a selected month.
formula_checks.rests_on: Written purpose and formula, on the stated valid input domain; ordinary arithmetic

formula_checks.name: pctBaseMonthly
formula_checks.why: Uses take-home after both tax and employee contributions as the common percentage base.
formula_checks.rests_on: Written purpose and formula, on the stated valid input domain; ordinary arithmetic

formula_checks.name: categoryMonthly
formula_checks.why: Normalizes a known category once; percent categories use the same annual-average take-home base and preserve the annual/monthly distinction.
formula_checks.rests_on: Written purpose and formula, on the stated valid input domain; ordinary arithmetic

formula_checks.name: spendBuckets
formula_checks.why: Aggregates explicitly normalized categories into fixed, non-monthly and flexible groups; fallback totals apply only without categories.
formula_checks.rests_on: Written purpose and formula, on the stated valid input domain; ordinary arithmetic

formula_checks.name: spendByMonthByBucket
formula_checks.why: Dated annual categories land only in their selected months; monthly remainder is added consistently and each bucket retains its identity.
formula_checks.rests_on: Written purpose and formula, on the stated valid input domain; ordinary arithmetic

formula_checks.name: spendByMonth
formula_checks.why: Sums the same three dated bucket amounts without doing a second allocation.
formula_checks.rests_on: Written purpose and formula, on the stated valid input domain; ordinary arithmetic

formula_checks.name: expenses
formula_checks.why: The approved drawing and formula can reconcile expenses, but linked-card payment exclusion differs from the actual flow contract, and repeated names can double-assign a payment.
formula_checks.should_be: Use stable debt identity and one stated treatment for card purchases versus balance payments, preserving section totals.

formula_checks.name: recurringDebtPayments
formula_checks.why: Applies each instalment payment’s start/payoff months and excludes revolving and due-in-full debt. Missing-payment disclosure remains the caller’s duty.
formula_checks.rests_on: Written purpose and formula, on the stated valid input domain; ordinary arithmetic

formula_checks.name: debtPaymentsCountedAsExpenses
formula_checks.why: Name-based payment matching can attach one expense to multiple debts with identical normalized names.
formula_checks.should_be: Require stable debt identity or flag ambiguous matches; a logged amount may be counted once.

formula_checks.name: actualSpending
formula_checks.why: Filters debt-payment expenses, source and month before sorting; shown and hidden subtotals reconcile. Inputs here are the month’s logs, not a claim that all spending was captured.
formula_checks.rests_on: Written purpose and formula, on the stated valid input domain; ordinary arithmetic

formula_checks.name: isRadarItem
formula_checks.why: Correctly separates instalment, revolving and due-in-full shapes.
formula_checks.rests_on: Written purpose and formula, on the stated valid input domain; ordinary arithmetic

formula_checks.name: radar
formula_checks.why: Known debt due/paid selection is coherent, but the prose does not establish the date window of bigBills or prevent showing a future bill as this month’s expense.
formula_checks.should_be: Declare bigBills input scope and filter dated bills to the queried month; do not treat a radar forecast as paid.

formula_checks.name: theBudgetCounted
formula_checks.why: Suppresses the named home mortgage category correctly, but does not identify any other debt duplicated in a user budget despite the broader any-debt rule.
formula_checks.should_be: Keep the home rule; require explicit debt links/exclusions for other duplicated debt categories and disclose any unresolved duplicates.

rules_held.decision_in_force: NOT A DECISION OF HIS — the lead's decision of 2026-10-23 under his rulings DEC-0002, DEC-0447 and DEC-0345, made without asking him, as his order of 2026-09-30 says. September with $700 of groceries and a $1,200 bill in December: This month −$700, the Expenses tab $700 (it read $800, with Once in a while $100), Home's September record $700. December: $1,900 on all three (Once in a while $1,200). A budget whose only line is the December bill reads $0 planned in September on both tabs — set, never "You haven't set your budget yet". A once-in-a-while bill with no month set is still a twelfth a month, as before. To reverse: build the Expenses tab's rows from the monthly average again. One word from him reverses it.

rules_held.decision_in_force: NOT A DECISION OF HIS — the lead's decision of 2026-10-24 under his rulings DEC-0002, DEC-0447, DEC-4529 and DEC-3523 (tenet 1), made without asking him, as his order of 2026-09-30 says. His $2,000 a month typed ($1,100 bills & fixed, $900 everyday) with $1,200 of car insurance in December: every month read $1,900, the typed $2,000 taken to hold $100 a month of the bill, and the $1,100 / $900 split was dropped. Now eleven months read $2,000 and December $3,200. Where a figure is a whole year shown by the month it counts the bill once: MK-CF-F-002, the planned monthly figure, 2,000 + 1,200 ÷ 12 = $2,100 (it read $2,000); MK-CF-F-009, the must-pay figure, $2,000 (it read $1,900). The Net worth emergency fund in the family-inputs household: (2,900 × 12 + 3,600) ÷ 12 + 4,670 = $7,870 (it read $7,570), $31,489 ÷ 6,070 = 5.2 months (it read 5.5). On his approved Net worth v08 drawing's household, $4,500 a month typed and a $3,600 April premium: the months of essentials read 2.1 ($8,838 ÷ $4,150; the drawing shows 2.3, from $3,850), and at the planned spend 1.8 ($5,050; the drawing shows 1.9, from $4,750). The drawing is left as drawn, with the correction line his DEC-4529 asks for in its READ THIS FIRST and the matching allowed difference in its test. Sign-up's recap reads MK-CF-F-002. No ruling of his says a typed budget already holds such a bill. To reverse: read the typed total as holding a twelfth of each dated bill again. One word from him reverses it.

rules_held.decision_in_force: NOT A DECISION OF HIS — the lead's decision of 2026-10-24 under his rulings DEC-1923 and DEC-3523 (tenets 1 and 4), made without asking him, as his order of 2026-09-30 says. One rule for a debt in a month, in two new shared functions, MK-CF-F-235 paysInMonth and MK-CF-F-236 paymentInMonth: from its first payment to its payoff, and a balance due in full once, in its month, at its balance. A $7,200 take-home, a $3,400 budget, the $2,400 mortgage, a $250 car loan whose first payment is Oct 28, a $300 loan paid off in August and a $1,000 tax bill due in full Sep 20: September's planned surplus read +$850, the car loan and the paid-off loan counted and the tax bill left out; it reads +$400 = 7,200 − 3,400 − 2,400 − 1,000, what the Bill calendar's September holds. October's card is unchanged, $1,150. ACTUAL no longer lists the car loan as due the 28th at $0; MONTHLY RECURRING EXPENSES reads $2,400 (it read $2,650); the tax bill is on the BIG-TICKET RADAR at $1,000; Home's due-soon reminder no longer fires for a loan not yet started. MK-CF-M-047, 048 and 049 now say they print on a later month's plan card, from the grid ($7,200 / $6,050 / $1,150), and the retired surplus line and the paycheck card's SURPLUS have their own number, MK-CF-M-078 (it printed under MK-CF-M-049). To reverse: count every debt's payment in this month again, whatever its dates. One word from him reverses it.
